system.name: DCP
system.one_liner: a dynamic context-parallel training framework that partitions attention data and computation into fine-grained blocks flexibly mapped to devices

content.subject: how attention blocks for a masked sequence are assigned to two devices under current methods versus DCP's balanced placement

elements.name: Q
elements.role: query block for one of 8 positions in the masked sequence (Q_1^1 ... Q_8^1), heading the left side of each staircase row

elements.name: C
elements.role: pairwise query-key computation block inside the attention triangle (C_1^1 ... C_24^1); some are omitted where the shared-question mask zeroes out attention

elements.name: KV
elements.role: key-value block along the base of the staircase, one per sequence position (KV_1^1 ... KV_8^1)

elements.name: O
elements.role: output block for one query row, drawn as a separate column at the far right (O_1^1 ... O_8^1)

elements.name: Device 0
elements.role: first device; receives an assigned subset of Q/KV/O data blocks and C computation blocks

elements.name: Device 1
elements.role: second device; receives the remaining subset of data and computation blocks

relations.what: each query block's row of computation blocks consumes it
each key-value block's column of computation blocks consumes it
a row's computation blocks combine into that row's output block
a placement strategy assigns each Q/KV/O block, and the C blocks it touches, to one of the two devices
computation blocks are likewise assigned to a device; current methods leave devices unevenly loaded while DCP balances them

panels.label: Placement of current methods
panels.differs: template: Device 0 receives the outer query/KV/output positions (1,2,7,8) and only 10 computation blocks, Device 1 receives the inner positions (3-6) and 14 computation blocks

panels.label: A possible placement under DCP
panels.differs: each device instead receives a mixed set of 4 query/KV/output triples drawn from across the sequence (e.g. device 0: positions 1,5,2,8), giving both devices exactly 12 computation blocks

values.what: which specific Q/KV/O/C block indices (1-8 for Q/KV/O, 1-24 for C) are assigned to Device 0 vs Device 1 under each placement
values.linked_by: position, grouped spatially into two stacked rows per device, plus shared orange/blue colour coding by block type
values.result_cells: the two block-list rows per device let the reader count and compare per-device totals directly

content.key_idea: Current methods assign attention blocks to devices by contiguous position, leaving devices with very different numbers of computation blocks; DCP instead reassigns blocks across the whole masked sequence so every device ends up with the same number of computation blocks.
content.reading_order: left to right through the staircase legend first, then top-to-bottom through the two current-method device rows, then the two DCP device rows below

palette.used_for: light peach fill of Q/KV/O (query, key-value, output) data blocks
gold-orange dashed border outlining each Q/KV/O block
light blue fill of C (pairwise computation) blocks
steel-blue dashed border outlining each C block

style.stroke: thin dashed borders, orange on Q/KV/O blocks and blue on C blocks
style.arrows: none; blocks are laid out by adjacency, not connected by drawn lines
style.font: italic serif math typesetting for the subscripted block labels; sans-serif for panel captions ('Device 0', 'Placement of current methods', ...)

encoding.color_means: orange marks query (Q), key-value (KV), and output (O) data blocks; blue marks the pairwise C computation blocks derived from them
encoding.state_means: the two placement panels are told apart purely by which block labels are grouped into each device's two rows; no highlighting marks the reassigned blocks directly
encoding.emphasis: the masked-out blank cells in the staircase and the very different Device-0/Device-1 C-block counts under current methods make the load imbalance visually obvious before DCP's balanced counts are shown
reusable_patterns: a staircase/triangular block grid as a shared legend for a masked-attention example, redrawn as flat per-device block lists under two competing placement policies
weaknesses: no arrows or colour highlighting mark exactly which block moved between the current-method and DCP placements, so the reader must compare the two per-device block lists by hand

Load balancing in DCP is achieved by assigning data/computation blocks that represent similar total data size

summary: Figure 11 illustrates how DCP's fine-grained blockwise partitioning improves on current placement methods for a masked attention sequence. The left legend shows the block structure for one shared-question-masked sequence: query blocks Q1-Q8 and key-value blocks KV1-KV8 generate 24 pairwise computation blocks C1-C24 arranged in a staircase, with three gaps where the mask zeroes out computation, plus one output block O per query row. On the right, 'Placement of current methods' assigns the outer query positions (1,2,7,8) to Device 0 (10 computation blocks) and the inner positions (3-6) to Device 1 (14 computation blocks), an uneven split. 'A possible placement under DCP' instead groups mixed query/KV/output triples from across the sequence onto each device, giving both devices exactly 12 computation blocks and balancing memory and compute.
summary_zh: 该图展示DCP的细粒度分块：左侧为带掩码序列的Q/KV/C/O分块楼梯图；右上现有方法按连续位置分配导致两设备计算块数不均(10 vs 14)；右下DCP按混合位置重新分配，使两设备各得12个计算块，负载均衡。
